## Request Context
- **What was requested**: Fix the ntfy collab loop so the developer can rely on it — a reply they tap on their phone must never be misfiled. Review the fix before commit.
- **Files/scope**: scripts/collab_loop.py (+81), tests/test_collab_loop.py (+124, 10 new tests incl. 3 @regression), .gitignore (+.collab_loop.lock).
- **Developer-stated motivation**: A real reply ('Approve build') was silently dropped (validated against a stale question's choices by a second concurrent poller). Developer needs the loop as reliable as typing; will manage autonomously over ntfy.
- **Explicit constraints**: Preserve the always-on untrusted-reply allow-list invariant; never print the topic slug; fix must be STRUCTURAL (not dependent on operator discipline). Single-poller lockfile + ask-retargets-choices design.

VERDICT: APPROVE (0.92). Fix preserves the always-on untrusted-reply allow-list invariant UNDER CONCURRENCY: poll calls lock_choices() per iteration before _emit, so a reply is always validated against the CURRENT question's choices; match_choice/_classify_reply_payload still sit between raw reply and any action; raw unmatched text never surfaced. Lockfile stores only {pid, choices, ts} — NO topic slug (confirmed). Fail-open is CORRECT here (lock is a coordination hint, not a security gate): missing/corrupt lock -> fall back to the poller's armed choices, never an unvalidated open-reply mode. Atomic tmp+replace write is right; except OSError: pass correct (a lock write must never crash the loop). PID-reuse not realistic for a long-lived interactive poller.
[ADVISORY Low] Shared-workstation only (NOT our single-user model): another OS user could write .collab_loop.lock in the repo root to inject a choices=[Approve build] allow-list. If ever multi-user/CI, move the lock to a user-private dir (/collab_loop_<uid>.lock). No action now.
[ADVISORY Low] update_lock_choices read-then-write race vs a concurrent claim_poll_lock could revert the pid -> new poller self-exits, no active poller (reliability, not security). Not reachable for one-ask-at-a-time usage; CAS-style update would close it. Document the assumption.

VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES (0.88). All 3 @regression tests FAIL under the old code + are non-tautological (verified the causal chain). Autouse _isolated_lock fixture is sound — LOCK_PATH resolved at call time so the monkeypatch sticks for new + pre-existing TestPoll/TestAsk tests (no real lockfile written to repo root). Injected-sleep synchronization for the supersede/retarget tests is deterministic, not flaky. Assertions are tight (exact per-iteration choice sequence, not no-raise).
[BLOCKING per confirmed-bug-fix standard, F2] Untested: a non-list  value in the lockfile (manual/corrupt edit) -> isinstance guard must fall back. ADDED test_lock_choices_non_list_value_falls_back.
[MEDIUM F3] Untested: write_lock OSError swallow (fail-open) — the worst silent path (poller arm-then-immediate-exit). ADDED test_write_lock_oserror_does_not_raise (no-raise + lock absent).
[ADVISORY F1] test_running_poller_adopts_retargeted_choices calls update_lock_choices directly (not via ask) — the ask->lockfile half is covered by test_ask_retargets_lock_choices; the two form a chain. Added cross-ref note.
[ADVISORY F4] Added a maintainer comment on the fixture: keep LOCK_PATH call-time-resolved (don't switch to a path=LOCK_PATH default arg, which freezes at import + breaks isolation).
[Low F5] supersede-test assertion meaningful + deterministic, no change.
All findings ADDRESSED in-session; 76 tests green.

## Request Context
- **What was requested**: Make the ntfy collab loop reliable (structural fix, not operator discipline) and review before commit.
- **Files/scope**: scripts/collab_loop.py (single-poller lockfile), tests/test_collab_loop.py (12 new tests, 3 regression), .gitignore.
- **Developer-stated motivation**: a real phone reply was silently misfiled by a stale concurrent poller; developer manages autonomously over ntfy and needs it as reliable as typing.
- **Explicit constraints**: preserve the untrusted-reply allow-list invariant; never print the topic slug; structural fix.

## Synthesis
Panel: security APPROVE 0.92, qa APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES 0.88. 0 BLOCKING on the design. Verified: the fix preserves the allow-list invariant under concurrency (poll validates against the lockfile's CURRENT choices each iteration), leaks no topic slug, and fail-open is the correct posture (a missing/corrupt lock falls back to the armed choices, never an unvalidated open mode). All 3 regression tests fail under the old code and are non-tautological; fixture isolation is sound. qa raised 2 quick hardening gaps, both ADDRESSED in-session: a non-list-choices fallback test and a write_lock OSError no-raise test (76 tests green). Plus maintainer comments (keep LOCK_PATH call-time-resolved; the ask->poller retarget is a two-test chain). Two security advisories accepted/scoped-out for the single-user local model (shared-workstation lock location; ask/claim read-then-write race) — documented, no action now. Ready to commit (NO push).
